incumbent.name: Greg Walker
incumbent.summary: Sen. Greg Walker (R-Columbus) has represented District 41 since 2006 {gwalker_bio}. He initially planned to retire, then sought a fifth term after the congressional redistricting fight, and lost the May 5, 2026 Republican primary to state Rep. Michelle Davis, so he will not be on the November ballot {ipm_walker_primary} {ipm_davis_wins}. The Senate Republican caucus lists him as chair of the Family and Children Services Committee {gwalker_bio}.
record: Committee roles, per the Senate Republican caucus: chair of Family and Children Services; ranking member of Elections and Ethics; member of Pensions and Labor and Public Policy; chaired the 2023 Interim Study Committee on Child Services {gwalker_bio}.

December 2025: Was among the 21 Senate Republicans who opposed the mid-decade congressional redistricting plan, which the Senate rejected 31–19; he described the effort as federal overreach {ipm_walker_primary} {ipm_davis_wins}.

Voted against the 2022 law removing the handgun permit requirement, a 2025 bill allowing partisan school board elections and a 2022 bill barring transgender girls from girls' school sports; he points to his votes for the near-total abortion ban and for restricting gender-transition care for minors {ipm_walker_primary}.
After the primary, he urged Davis to "serve the people of the district. Serve them all, Republican, Democrat, Independent" {ipm_davis_wins}.

race_context: District 41 includes all of Bartholomew County and much of Johnson County {ipm_walker_primary} {gwalker_bio}. Bartholomew County cast about 62% of the votes in the 2022 primary and general elections for the seat {ipm_walker_primary}.

Open seat in November: incumbent Greg Walker lost renomination. In the May 5, 2026 Republican primary, Davis received 7,314 votes (58.8%) to Walker's 5,134 (41.2%), per Wikipedia's compilation; the AP called the race for Davis {wiki_2026_in_senate} {ipm_davis_wins}.

The primary centered on redistricting: Davis voted for the House plan and was endorsed by President Trump, while Walker opposed it; outside groups including a group aligned with U.S. Sen. Jim Banks, the Club for Growth and Americans for Prosperity backed Davis {ipm_walker_primary}.
Democrat Ross Thomas was unopposed for his party's nomination {ipm_walker_primary}. WFIU described the district as historically Republican {ipm_davis_wins}.
No general-election debate or forum between Davis and Thomas was found in reviewed coverage.

candidates.summary: Davis is a three-term state representative from Whiteland (House District 58, since 2020) and director of adult education at Central Nine Career Center who defeated Sen. Walker in the Republican primary {ipm_walker_primary} {ipm_davis_wins}.
background: Director of adult education at Central Nine Career Center in Greenwood and owner of a local outdoor storage lot, per the House Republican caucus {davis_bio}.
Played Division I basketball at Ball State University, where she earned an elementary education degree, and holds a master's in curriculum and instruction from Purdue {ipm_davis_wins}.

In the House, she is assistant majority floor leader and vice chair of the Education Committee and serves on Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development and Judiciary, per the caucus {davis_bio}. Lives in Whiteland {davis_bio}.
path_to_ballot: Filed Jan. 7, 2026 {jc_filings}; won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 58.8% over incumbent Greg Walker {wiki_2026_in_senate} {ipm_davis_wins}.

items: Voted for the 2025 congressional redistricting bill in the House and said "the Senate should have stepped up and done the right thing for Hoosiers" {ipm_walker_primary}; argued the previous maps did not reflect that most Hoosiers are conservative {ipm_davis_wins}.
Authored House Enrolled Act 1195 (2026), expanding eligibility for and extending the high school equivalency pilot program to mid-2028 {davis_hea1195}.
Authored House Enrolled Act 1041 (2025), barring transgender women from women's collegiate sports {davis_hea1041}.
Co-sponsored Senate Bill 76 (2026), requiring local governments to comply with federal immigration detainer requests: "Public safety depends on cooperation at every level of government" {davis_sb76}.
Authored a 2024 law requiring mental health resources after school armed-intruder drills and making school resource officers eligible for the 1977 Pension Fund {davis_sro}.
Authored 2023 laws doubling juror pay to $80 a day and allowing 25% of state adult education funding to go to integrated education and workforce training {davis_jury} {davis_adulted}.

on_incumbent: Said her and Walker's voting records had "key differences" and described herself as the more conservative candidate: "I will always vote for morals and for what the Hoosier families believe in" {ipm_walker_primary}. No statements about Thomas were found.
plans: No published general-election agenda was found in reviewed coverage.
endorsements_finance: Endorsed by President Trump in the primary {ipm_davis_wins} {ipm_walker_primary}.
Her campaign reported raising $115,000 for the Senate race as of late April 2026; pro-redistricting groups spent at least several hundred thousand dollars on ads supporting her {ipm_walker_primary}.
gaps: Search snippets report endorsements from U.S. Sen. Jim Banks, Gov. Braun, Treasurer Daniel Elliott, AFP, NRA-PVF and Turning Point Action, and that her website highlights school choice, Second Amendment support and ending abortion (Capital Chronicle voter guide, inaccessible); unverified.
Her House votes on the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) and 2025 budget not verified.
Campaign website not located; her campaign canceled a scheduled interview with the Capital Chronicle {ipm_walker_primary}.

candidates.summary: Thomas is an attorney and chair of the Bartholomew County Democratic Party who was unopposed for the Democratic nomination; he previously ran for this seat in 2018 {wiki_2026_in_senate} {ipm_walker_primary}.
background: An attorney and chair of the Bartholomew County Democratic Party; was the Democratic candidate for this seat in 2018 and for Indiana House District 59 in 2022 and 2024, per Wikipedia {wiki_2026_in_senate}.
path_to_ballot: Filed Jan. 7, 2026 {jc_filings}; unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary {ipm_walker_primary}.
on_incumbent: No statements by Thomas about Walker's record, Davis or the seat's direction were found in reviewed coverage.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising totals were found in reviewed coverage.
gaps: Very limited verified coverage. Search snippets of the Indiana Capital Chronicle voter guide (inaccessible) say his campaign website highlights public education investment, a moratorium on new large-scale data centers, abortion rights, marijuana legalization and Statehouse ethics reform, that he has his own law firm in Indianapolis, and that he did not return the guide's tax survey; unverified.
The Republic (Columbus) articles, including on a Hoosier Action candidate town hall, were inaccessible (403).
